what_i_did: The turnaround's left/middle/right panels are front/side/back as labelled, but the bright floor glow and soft floor shadows were being counted as object in the target masks (the front mask spanned the full panel width). views/ holds copies with the floor below the base and the low-chroma floor shadows painted to background; all scores use score r views.

Built the T-post on a two-layer plank base, the lashed crossbeam with chunky end caps and a raised centre hump, the Y-shaped knee braces, the pointed iron finial, and two shallow pans each on one hanger rope that splits into three cords at a knot.

The beam is its own object pivoting on a bronze pin held between two carved yoke cheeks on the post top. Each hanger (rope, knot, three cords, pan) is a child of the beam with its origin at the tie-on point, and is keyed with the exact opposite angle on the same frames, so the pans stay plumb on every frame.

Bevelled, slightly jittered timbers, a rope collar binding the post foot with a loose rope tail and coil on the base, rope lashings at both hang points and around the beam centre, rolled pan rims with a lighter bronze inside, and a bronze pin head.
All three animated objects share one action, exported with export_anim_scene_split_object=False so the GLB carries a single 120-frame clip instead of one clip per object.

Moved the proportions toward the hero illustration (taller and more open, bigger and deeper pans, a broad, thick plank base with the stone resting on it), added the four-turn rope wrap on the post foot and knotted beam-end lashings as low-poly torus rings, and gave every bevelled edge a darker chamfer material so the wood reads two-tone. Still flat colours, no textures.
good: Front and side silhouettes line up well: crossbeam, Y braces, finial, hanger knots and pan rims sit where the sheet has them (side 0.72 IoU; front 0.61 after the hero-led round 9).
The motion reads clearly: the beam tips 6.5 degrees one way, 5.5 the other, then damps out over 100 frames, and the finial needle rides with the beam so it acts as the pointer.
Verified after re-importing the GLB: the hangers' world rotation is 0 at frames 1, 16, 36, 60 and 120.
2,950 triangles, just under the 3k budget, in 5 meshes: stand, beam, hanger_left, hanger_right, stone_weights.
Real scale: 1.16 m tall at the finial tip, 0.99 m across the pans, origin at the centre of the footprint on the ground, front faces -Y.
off: The back view is the weakest at 0.57 IoU. The sheet draws the back with an asymmetric perspective (the beam and pans sit off-centre), which one symmetric model can't match on both front and back.

The stones contradict each other: the sheet's front view puts them in front of the base, its side view puts them behind, and the hero puts a single big stone on top of the base. I followed the hero (a stone on the base, front-left) and put the small weight stack behind the base, where the side view shows it.
The hero's beam passes through a mortise below a carved post cap. I used the sheet's beam-on-top layout with yoke cheeks, because a beam fixed in a mortise couldn't tip.
Round 9 deliberately follows the hero over the sheet: the stand is wider and the pans bigger than the orthographic sheet, so mean IoU went from 0.652 to 0.626.
The timber is still flat colour with darker chamfers. The illustration's carved grain and split end-grain would need textures or many more triangles.

rounds.change: First full build: plank base, T-post, beam with hump and caps, thin diagonal braces, weight stones on the ground in front of the base.
Moved the weight stack behind the base (matching the side view) and the big stone onto the base (matching the hero), made the braces and beam thicker, and darkened the timber.
Raised the beam, pivot, braces and pans by 4 cm (the upper body was squashed compared with the sheet) and narrowed the base.

Replaced the box braces with knee-brace prisms that flare toward the beam (the sheet's Y shape), with stop pads on top. Also tried a shorter beam, shallower and higher pans, and a deeper base; those three made it worse.
Kept the new braces and reverted beam length, pan height and base depth. Moved the animation into a single shared action.
Colour pass: browner timber, darker bronze pan shells, duller rope, and a larger hero stone. Mean colour distance dropped from about 0.19 to 0.10.
Tried a thicker post and beam. The post helped the back view, but the thicker beam would hit the braces at full tilt, so I kept the post and reverted the beam. No net gain, so I stopped.
Final 768 px, 48-sample render of the round 7 model (brace tops lowered 4 mm for clearance).

Art director round, aimed at the hero rather than the sheet. Taller and more open: pivot 0.89 to 0.98 m, beam 0.71 to 0.82 m, hang points at 0.27 to 0.33 m. Bigger, deeper pans: 0.32 m bowls (39% of the beam) 9 cm deep, rims 0.40 m up (34% of the height). Base is a broad, thick two-layer plank slab, 0.50 x 0.44 x 0.136 m, wider front to back than the pans, with a larger grey stone on it beside the post. The post foot has a four-turn rope wrap, and each beam end has three-turn lashings with a knot plus a two-turn binding on the cap. Darker chamfer material on every bevel (two-tone timber) and a lighter centre plank on the base. Final 768 px / 48 samples. IoU fell from 0.652 to 0.626 because the sheet draws a narrower stand; mean colour distance fell to about 0.07.

moving_parts: One 120-frame clip at 24 fps that loops seamlessly (rest pose at frames 1 and 102-120). The beam rocks about its bronze pin (local Y axis at z = 0.98 m): +6.5 degrees at f16, -5.5 at f36, +3.5 at f53, -2.0 at f68, +1.0 at f81, -0.35 at f92, then 0 from f102. hanger_left and hanger_right are children of the beam, pivoting at their tie-on points, and are keyed with the exact negative angle on the same frames and interpolation, so the pans swing up and down on the beam ends but always hang straight down. The iron finial is part of the beam and acts as the pointer needle.
creative_additions: The knee braces double as tilt stops: their pads sit just under the beam, so at full tilt the beam nearly touches them, which explains why the swing is limited. I added a bronze pivot pin through carved yoke cheeks, rope lashings at each hang point, little binding knots on every cord, rolled pan rims with a lighter bronze inner face, a rope collar and loose rope tail with a coil at the post foot (from the hero), and a stack of flat stone weights behind the base for the merchant.
